citations.narrative:
During the inspection, an incident involving the escape and subsequent capture of an elk was reviewed. On May 19,
2026, a female elk escaped its enclosure through the main gate which had inadvertently been left open by a facility staff
member. The following morning, the elk was observed in another location within the park, and the animal was quickly
immobilized in order to return it to its enclosure. During the immobilization and movement of the large animal, it sustained
superficial wounds which were quickly addressed by the facility's attending veterinarian.
Failure to secure enclosures can allow for the escape of animals which can cause behavioral stress and physical harm
while the animal is able to freely roam throughout the facility and during attempts to capture the animal.
Handling of all animals shall be done as expeditiously and carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma,
overheating, behavioral stress, physical harm, or unnecessary discomfort. Ensure that facility enclosures are kept secure
to prevent escape and unnecessary stress involved with capture.
Corrected prior to the inspection on 22-June-2026.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
An individually housed spider monkey, in an outdoor enclosure, is unable to see and hear other nonhuman primates. The
AV had approved the environmental enhancement plan when there were two cohoused spider monkeys, but the plan has
not been updated since the animal has been individually housed. The current plan does not adequately address the
special considerations for the singly housed nonhuman primate that is unable to see and hear its own or compatible
species. Failure to ensure that the environmental enhancement plan addresses special considerations and to ensure that
the plan is implemented accordingly can lead to psychological distress and prolonged discomfort. Correct by ensuring that
the environmental enhancement plan addresses special considerations and is approved by the attending veterinarian.
Correct by, 10-July-2026.

The enclosure housing four domestic cattle and one yak have excessively muddy conditions primarily on the right side of
the enclosure. There is standing water and mud surrounding the water receptacle. The shelters and livestock feeder also
had mud and puddling of water around them. The animals in the enclosure are required to walk through and stand in
these wet areas to access water and shelter. Failure to provide adequate drainage in hoof stock enclosures can lead to
disease conditions in the hooves of the animals which can result in lameness or reluctance to move. Additionally, the
geriatric animals housed in the enclosure may have more difficulty traversing the wet environment. Correct by ensuring
that a suitable method is provided to rapidly eliminate excess water. The method of drainage shall comply with applicable
Federal, State, and local laws and regulations relating to pollution control or the protection of the environment. Correct by,
24-July-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
AMY NOOYEN, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
